svg.text: Euclid steps across the base plane while preserving the fiber
Each step (x, y) ↦ (y, x mod y) moves to a simpler base point with the exact same fiber Div(x) ∩ Div(y)
1. Base Plane (x, y) ∈ [0..21]²: Level Sets of Equal Fiber
Bottom row y = 0 is the stopping boundary where Gcd(x, 0) = {x}
state x (at y = 0, return x ∈ Gcd(x, 0) = {x}) →
2. Dependent Type Equality Along Each Euclid Step
Theorem: Div(x) ∩ Div(y) = Div(y) ∩ Div(x mod y) ⇒ Gcd(x,y) = Gcd(y, x mod y)
At y = 0: x = 4 ∈ Gcd(4, 0) = Gcd(8, 4) = Gcd(12, 8) (Q.E.D. without extra proof!)
Worst-case Fibonacci inputs step across 7 base points, all sharing fiber {1}:
Div(21) ∩ Div(13) = {1,3,7,21} ∩ {1,13} = {1} = Div(1), so fiber is {1} throughout.
Origin Fiber (0, 0): Why Gcd(0, 0) = {0} Without Special Cases
• Every natural d divides 0 (since 0 = 0 · d), so Div(0) = ℕ.
• At (0, 0): Div(g) = Div(0) ∩ Div(0) = ℕ, holding ONLY for g = 0.
• Thus Gcd(0, 0) = {0} is the unique fiber inhabited by 0.
